gen-fs-bevellier-gf-noto-sans-elymaic: Noto Sans Elymaic keeps its apertures open and its ascenders hugging the x-height, plain sans through and through. Bevellier is the one with the flat, stencil-cut line of a single pen width, while the body just gets on with being legible.
gen-fs-bevellier-gf-noto-sans-ethiopic: Graceful and a bit severe, Bevellier runs one stroke width through the whole alphabet above the sturdy, tall-bodied Noto Sans Ethiopic. Its c terminals hang far from the bowl.
gen-fs-bevellier-gf-noto-sans-georgian: Bevellier has no thick-thin flicker to catch the eye, just flat, close-set letters. Noto Sans Georgian slips underneath with open curves and short ascender stems, so the sophisticated heading and the modern sans text sit together without any fuss.
gen-fs-bevellier-gf-noto-sans-glagolitic: Flat, tight and signage-plain: that is Bevellier, with squat ascenders on a wide-looking lowercase. Noto Sans Glagolitic is its friendly counterweight, a plain sans whose round, open letters stay clear at small sizes.
gen-fs-bevellier-gf-noto-sans-gothic: Bevellier looks marker-drawn, flat and stencil-cut, with letters packed very close together. Noto Sans Gothic, a plain sans with huge round counters, would read in an easy, open way over a whole page.
gen-fs-bevellier-gf-noto-sans-gujarati: Noto Sans Gujarati reads clean and modern, with large open counters in its tall a, e and s. Over a full page, Noto Sans Gujarati stays a sans of curved strokes that end before they turn inward, while Bevellier's stress-free curves sit above it.
gen-fs-bevellier-gf-noto-sans-gunjala-go: Dowel-straight stems and bent-dowel arcs give Bevellier a sophisticated, stencil-flat look. Yet Noto Sans Gunjala Gondi, a plain sans with crayon-thick strokes and terminals cut well back, supplies the looser, contemporary texture underneath.
gen-fs-bevellier-gf-noto-sans-gurmukhi: Noto Sans Gurmukhi reads clean and professional, its terminals pointing outward like tongs and its ascenders barely clearing the x-height. Bevellier above it has no quill-style tapering at all, only flat single-weight strokes, which gives the plain sans below a quiet partner.
gen-fs-bevellier-gf-noto-sans-hebrew: Noto Sans Hebrew reads professional and modern, with a dominant midsection and wide gaps between curve ends and stems. Its strongest quality is the contrast with Bevellier, whose strokes are like cut ribbon of constant width, flat, graceful and stencil-tight.
gen-fs-bevellier-gf-noto-sans-hk: Bevellier draws with the steady line of a technical drafting pen. Beneath it, Noto Sans HK, a plain sans with large lowercase forms and lifted brush ends, gives that flat, tight heading a roomier, clean companion.
